ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (38) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

«Добро» (dobro, 'good') and «благо» (blago, 'a good, the good') are kept distinct (Seneca: 'Life is not always a good'). «Клеовуд» (Kleovud) is taken as Cleobulus, and the line about the crafty person, printed after the attribution «Восточная мудрость» (Vostochnaya mudrost', 'Eastern wisdom') and outside the quotation, is translated where it stands.

Source observation: [23] the line «С человеком лукавым не затягивайся в спор…» evidently belongs to the Eastern-wisdom list of no. 4 but is printed after the attribution and outside the blockquote (across the page break); translated where printed
Source observation: [30] «Клеовуд» (Kleovud) looks like a slip for «Клеовул» (Kleovul), Cleobulus; rendered 'Cleobulus'
